The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 23.05.2024.
2.

The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that, on 23.05.2024 at about 07.00 p.m., the petitioner was walking by the side of the road along with his mother, observing the traffic rules,
proceeding on Bidarahalli-Byyappanahalli, Bengaluru East Taluk, Bengaluru, at that time a motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HJ-5806 ridden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner, without following any traffic rules, came at a high speed and dashed to the petitioner.
Due to forced impact, petitioner fell down and sustained several grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.

Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to East Point Hospital and admitted as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.
The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident she was heal and healthy and aged about 11 years, studying in Government School.

Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and he cannot do his activities as earlier to the accident and undergoing deep mental shock,
pain and suffering.
Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, the Manoj vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197471455/
2 petitioner has filed this petition for compensation of Rs.20,00,000/-
with interest.

sentences.text: 3. After service of notice, respondent No.2 remained absent before the Court.
Hence, placed exparte.

The respondent No.1 in its written statement denied the allegations made in the plaint and submitted that, this respondent issued the policy to the offending vehicle and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.

It is further submitted that, the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HJ-5806 was not at all involved in the accident and the rider of the alleged vehicle was no way related in the alleged accident as on the date of the accident.
This respondent being the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HJ-5806 was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.

Further, this respondent emphatically denies the occurrence and mode of the accident and also involvement of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.
KA-53-HJ-5806 as mentioned in the claim petition.

Further this respondent denied the age,
occupation and income of the petitioner.
The petitioner colluding with the police filed the false case.
By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.
4. On the basis of above pleadings, following issues are framed:

1 . Whether the petitioner proves that, he is the victim of the motorcycle bearing Reg.
No. KA- 53-HJ-5806 on 23.05.2024 at about 07.00 p.m., on Bidarahalli- Byyappanahalli road, Bangalore East Taluk, Bengaluru and sustained injuries as pleaded in the petition?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What order or Award?
5. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, natural guardian i.e., mother of petitioner is examined as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and examined Dr. Nagaraj. B. N as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.14 and Ex.P.15 and also examined MRO at East Point Hospital as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P.16 to Ex.P.18 and closed their side.
On the other hand, no evidence is lead on behalf of the respondents.

6. Heard arguments of both the sides and perused the materials placed on record.
7.

Issue No.3 : As per final order,

sentences.text: 8. ISSUE No.1:

The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
9. The natural guardian of the petitioner i.e., his mother is examined as PW.1 by reiterating the averments made in the petition.
She has produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to 13.

Ex.P.1 is the FIR,
Ex.P.2 is the Complaint, Ex.P.3 is the MLC Report, Ex.P.4 is the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.5 is the Seizer Mahazar, Ex.P.6 is the IMV Report, Ex.P.7 is the Wound Certificate, Ex.P.8 is the Notice U/s 133 of M. V. Act, Ex.P.9 is the Reply Notice, Ex.P.10 is the Charge-sheet, Ex.P.11 is the Medica Bills,
Ex.P.12 is the Notarized copy of Aadhar Card of PW.1 and Ex.P.13 is the Notarized copy of Aadhar Card of petitioner.
10. The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent riding by the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53- HJ-5806.

Ex.P.1 to 10 are the only documents,
which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of riding of the rider of offending vehicle.

The Ex.P.4 (Spot Mahazar), clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information, held investigation and filed the Ex.P.10, Charge-Sheet against the rider of offending vehicle U/s. 279 and 338 of IPC R/w Sec. 187 of the M. V. Act.
The Ex.
P.6 i.e.
, certified copy of the IMV Report discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles in question.

11. It must be noted that, in the cross- examination of PW.1, it is suggested by the learned counsel for respondent No.1 that, the accident had not happened because of the negligence on the part of rider of the motorcycle, but witness denied the said suggestion.
No matter whether PW.1 admits the said suggestion or not, but in my opinion, the said suggestion is sufficient to conclude that,
respondent No.1 has admitted the accident
. In other words, it is well settled that, suggestion is the reflection of the case of the opponent.

Therefore, in my view, by posing a suggestion to the effect that, the accident had occurred because of the negligence of the rider of motorcycle, the respondent No.1 has admitted that, the accident in question had happened.
12. The next question would be, on whose fault accident has occurred.

This question arises because at para No.9 of the written statement filed by respondent No.1, in which the respondent No.1 has raised the specific defence that, the accident had happened due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.
Thus, the question would be whether this say of the respondent No.1 can be accepted or not.

It is true that, in the cross-examination of petitioner/PW.1, learned counsel for respondent No.1 has posed question to the PW.1 that, accident is happened due to the negligence of petitioner himself,
but PW.1 had denied the said suggestion.
However, it is important to note that, the second respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle remained absent despite service of notice.
Except denial and suggestion insurance company has not furnished any evidence to show the negligence on the part of the petitioner.

sentences.text: It is true that, petitioner has filed complaint against the rider of the offending motorcycle on 10.07.2024 i.e., after 45 days from the date of incident.
This tribunal opine that, treatment of the victim is given priority over lodging of FIR and delay of lodging of FIR cannot be ground to deny the justice to the claimants.

This view of this tribunal receives support from decisions of Hon'ble Apex Court as well as High Court which are reported in, 2022 ACJ 2482 between United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Sahanaz Bibi and others, 2022 ACJ 170 between Venkatesha K. N Vs. Thipregowda and others and 2011 ACJ 2350 between Bangalore Metropolitan Transport Corporation Vs. Pullaiah.
Moreover, as per the MLC Report at Ex.P.3, East Point Hospital authorities has issued Police Intimation on the date of accident itself i.e., on 23.05.2024 and concerned police have received the intimation on the day itself at 09.30 p.m.,

sentences.text: Once the police have received the intimation, the they ought to rush to the hospital to proceed further.

Moreover, complainant herself in her complaint mentioned the reasons for delay in lodging the first information and she also explained in her cross-examination, the reasons for non-filing of the complaint immediately.
So, in view of above facts and circumstances, delay caused in filing of the First Information before the concerned police does not itself dis-entitle the claim from the respondent.
14. The next question would be, whether the petitioner sustained injuries in the accident or not.
It must be noted that, the Ex.P.7 i.e., Wound Certificate shows that, the petitioner was admitted to East Point Hospital on 23.05.2024 with alleged history of RTA.
Further, Wound Certificate shows that, the injury sustained by the petitioner is grievous in nature.
These facts are not denied by the Respondent No.1.

Hence, these facts are sufficient to conclude that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.
KA-53-HJ-5806.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE No.2:
Before proceeding on merits of the claim the age of the petitioner/injured has to be determined.
Ex.P.13 is the Aadhar Card of the petitioner, wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 01.01.2013 and accident took place in the year 2024.
Accordingly, I assess his age as 11 years at the time of this accident.

Before going to discuss this issue, it is appropriate to reproduce the certain paragraphs of Judgment reported in NC:2025:KHC-K:3234 between Sagar Vs. Umesh.
"21.
It is not only the notional income of a minor which was involved.
Even the Multiplier was also the subject matter of these decisions.

Initially, the Multiplier of '15' was considered for the minor aged 18 years as per the Schedule II of the M. V.
Act, 1988.

Thereafter, in the case of Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and others, the Apex Court held that the multiplier suggested in the Schedule is incorrect and laid down that the multiplier should be '18' for the age group of 15 to 25 years.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, it did not suggest any multiplier for the age below 15 years.

Later, in the case of Kajal Vs. Jagadish Chand and others, referred supra and in the case of Master Ayush Vs. The Branch Manager, (2009) 6 SCC 121] NC:
2025:KHC-K:3234 HC-KAR Reliance General Insurance Co.,Ltd., and another21, the Apex Court adopted the multiplier of '18' for the minors aged 11 years and 12 years.

entities.text: Kajal Vs. Jagadish Chand and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Master Ayush Vs. The Branch Manager, (2009) 6 SCC 121]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, adopting the multiplier was also considered for the age group of below 15 years.

sentences.text: There cannot be any justification to adopt a multiplier which is less than '18' for minors.
23. Therefore, after considering the imponderables of life expectancy, the maximum multiplier of '18' is prescribed.
There is no reason as to why a child below '15' years is to be considered with a lesser multiplier than '18'.
Therefore, what can be inferred is that the multiplier for the age group below 15 is also to be considered as '18' only.
34.The
guidelines issued by the KSLSA for the purpose of settlement of disputes before the Lok- adalat prescribe a notional income of Rs.13,250/- per month for the year 2019.

In umpteen number of judgments including the judgment in the case of Smt.Mariyamma and others referred supra, this Court has held that the guidelines issued by KSLSA are in general conformity with the wages fixed under the Minumum Wages Act."

The method of calculation of the compensation in case of minor is also followed in the subsequent Judgment reported in NC:2025:KHC-K:3233 between Neekitha Vs. Sharanagouda, wherein laid down following points while calculating the compensation in case of minor:
(a) the income of the minor has to be the notional income, which is relatable to the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act,
(b) the Multiplier to be applied is '18' irrespective of the age of the minor, and (c) the future prospects have to be added if the functional disability is above 50%.
However, if the evidence shows that the child was having excellent academic or other prowess, the above rule may be deviated to compensate the child adequately.

16. In the instant case, the natural guardian of petitioner in her evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to East Point Hospital, Bangalore, wherein he took treatment as inpatient from 17.06.2025 to 23.06.2025 i.e., for totally 06 days.

She has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.7, which reveals that, petitioner has sustained the following injuries:
(i) Fracture of Tibia and fibula  leg.
(ii) Lacrotion over the fore-head - 4x2 cm.
(iii) Punched lacretion over the medical mcolleolus (iv) Abrasion 10x4 cm  leg.
The petitioner to prove his disability, he has produced the evidence of Dr. Nagaraj. B. N as PW.2 who has produced documents marked at Ex.P.14 and Ex.P.15.
Admittedly, the PW.2 is not a treated doctor.

He was sworn that, petitioner has got Disability of 13% to the whole body, but he has not Manoj vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197471455/
6 issued the disability certificate.

entities.text: Manoj vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: During cross examination PW.2 admits that, fracture is united and implants are removed.
Further he also admits that, disability percentage of petitioner may come down in future and petitioner is not having any difficulty to attend School.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor and evidence given by the petitioner himself before the Court, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having functional disability to the extent of 8%, cannot be ruled out.
Therefore, this Tribunal consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 8%.

As per the ruling reported in NC:2025:KHC- K:3233 between Neekita Vs. Sharanagouda and another, the relevant multiplier applicable is '18' and Notional Income of petitioner is considered as Rs.16,500/-.
Under this head the petitioner is entitled for an amount of Rs.2,76,480/-.
17. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

In the petition as well as in his evidence PW.1 deposed that, after the accident she was shifted to East Point Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient from 17.06.2025 to 23.06.2025 i.e., for totally 06 days.
PW.1 has also produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.7, which reveals that, petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Hence, it is clear that during the above said period the petitioner suffered lot of pain and inconvenience.
Considering all these aspects this tribunal has granted Rs.30,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
18. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
However in support of his plea, he has produced medical bills which is marked at Ex.P.11 to the tune of Rs.32,305/-.
Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.32,305/- towards medical expenses.
19. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID UP PERIOD:
The petitioner has pleaded that, he took treatment in East Point Hospital as inpatient from 17.06.2025 to 23.06.2025 for about 06 days.
Hence, at least 01 month is required to recover from the accidental injuries.
The income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,500/- p.m. as per above decision.
Hence, 01 month is to be considered as loss of income.
Hence, she is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,500/- under this head.
20. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The petitioner was aged about 11 years at the time of accident, he has sustained grievous injuries.
However he might have suffered lot of pain and loss of amenities and comforts in life.
Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries and fracture, Rs.20,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
1 Pain and sufferings Rs. 30,000/-
2

Medical expenses Rs. 32,305/-

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,75,285/- under various heads.
21. LIABILITY:

As discussed in Issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HJ-5806 and the police have conducted due enquiry and filed charge sheet against the said driver of the offending vehicle punishable U/s 279 and 339 of IPC.
From perusal of the policy, the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.1 for the period from 24.04.2022 to 23.04.2027.
Admittedly, the accident in question took place on 23.05.2024.
Hence, policy was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, respondent No.1 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.2 owner.
22. INTEREST:

As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
By relying on the aforesaid decision,
6% interest awarded to the petitioners in the present case on hand. Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
23. ISSUE No.3:

In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER:
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I.M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is awarded with  compensation of Rs.3,75,285/- with  interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of  petition till its realization.

No. KA- 53-HJ-5806 on 23.05.2024 at about 07.00 p.m., on Bidarahalli- Byyappanahalli road, Bangalore East Taluk, Bengaluru and sustained injuries as pleaded in the petition?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or Award?
5. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, natural guardian i.e., mother of petitioner is examined as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and examined Dr. Nagaraj. B. N as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.14 and Ex.P.15 and also examined MRO at East Point Hospital as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P.16 to Ex.P.18 and closed their side.
12. The next question would be, on whose fault accident has occurred.
14. The next question would be, whether the petitioner sustained injuries in the accident or not.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
10. The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent riding by the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53- HJ-5806.
The Ex.P.4 (Spot Mahazar), clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information, held investigation and filed the Ex.P.10, Charge-Sheet against the rider of offending vehicle U/s. 279 and 338 of IPC R/w Sec. 187 of the M. V. Act.
Therefore, in my view, by posing a suggestion to the effect that, the accident had occurred because of the negligence of the rider of motorcycle, the respondent No.1 has admitted that, the accident in question had happened.
Manoj vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197471455/
4 13.
It is true that, petitioner has filed complaint against the rider of the offending motorcycle on 10.07.2024 i.e., after 45 days from the date of incident.
This tribunal opine that, treatment of the victim is given priority over lodging of FIR and delay of lodging of FIR cannot be ground to deny the justice to the claimants.
This view of this tribunal receives support from decisions of Hon'ble Apex Court as well as High Court which are reported in, 2022 ACJ 2482 between United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Sahanaz Bibi and others, 2022 ACJ 170 between Venkatesha K. N Vs. Thipregowda and others and 2011 ACJ 2350 between Bangalore Metropolitan Transport Corporation Vs. Pullaiah.
Moreover, as per the MLC Report at Ex.P.3, East Point Hospital authorities has issued Police Intimation on the date of accident itself i.e., on 23.05.2024 and concerned police have received the intimation on the day itself at 09.30 p.m.,
Once the police have received the intimation, the they ought to rush to the hospital to proceed further.
So, in view of above facts and circumstances, delay caused in filing of the First Information before the concerned police does not itself dis-entitle the claim from the respondent.
Hence, these facts are sufficient to conclude that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.
KA-53-HJ-5806.
Thereafter, in the case of Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and others, the Apex Court held that the multiplier suggested in the Schedule is incorrect and laid down that the multiplier should be '18' for the age group of 15 to 25 years.
Later, in the case of Kajal Vs. Jagadish Chand and others, referred supra and in the case of Master Ayush Vs. The Branch Manager, (2009) 6 SCC 121] NC:
2025:KHC-K:3234 HC-KAR Reliance General Insurance Co.,Ltd., and another21, the Apex Court adopted the multiplier of '18' for the minors aged 11 years and 12 years.
Manoj vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197471455/
5
Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor and evidence given by the petitioner himself before the Court, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having functional disability to the extent of 8%, cannot be ruled out.
Admittedly, the accident in question took place on 23.05.2024.
Hence, policy was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, respondent No.1 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.2 owner.
As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.
